source.title: The Dragon Hatchling: The Missing Link between the Transformer and Models of the Brain
source.authors: A. Kosowski; Przemyslaw Uznanski; J. Chorowski; Zuzanna Stamirowska; M. Bartoszkiewicz

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports related findings on BDH-GPU activation sparsity and semantically selective synapses, but does not test feature superposition, capacity-driven polysemanticity, SAE features, or feature dimensionality as defined by the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The reported BDH-GPU sparsity and synapse-selectivity measurements are recorded as related findings under fits_no_version. They do not measure superposition geometry or capacity competition, nor do they test SAE recovery or canonical feature units. Comparisons with GPTXL and graph baselines, and values used to choose thresholds, do not establish the claim.
record.test_reason: The paper introduces the BDH/BDH-GPU architecture and reports activation sparsity, modular weight graphs and selected 'monosemantic' synapses in that architecture. It never measures feature directions vs. dimensions, superposition geometry, capacity competition, SAE recovery or feature dimensionality, and it does not cite or test Toy Models of Superposition. Its monosemanticity result is a property claimed for a purpose-built architecture, found by selecting synapses with predictive power. It is not a measurement of whether superposition or polysemanticity arises in standard networks.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also frame sparse positive activations and monosemantic synapses as built-in interpretability advantages of BDH over the Transformer. They do not frame these as tests of superposition or SAE claims. They additionally report emergent modular, heavy-tailed weight graphs and Transformer-like scaling.
record.recipe_differences: No superposition experiment or original-method reproduction is reported; the paper introduces and evaluates the BDH/BDH-GPU architecture.
record.method_sensitivity: The synthetic activation experiment reports different sparsity during memorization and repetition; the synapse-selectivity result compares currency-related with politics contrast sentences.

fits_no_version.finding: A BDH-GPU attention-state entry, selected for predictive power, takes higher values on currency sentences than on politics contrasts (U=2368/2500, rank-biserial 0.86). It responds across English and French.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In BDH-GPU, individual synapse-state entries can be selectively associated with a semantic concept across languages.

fits_no_version.finding: BDH-GPU activations are sparse (~5%). Layer-2 activity falls from 4.0–7.5% nonzero during memorization to ~2.5% during repetition.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: BDH-GPU neuron activation sparsity increases as input becomes more predictable.

record.problems: The synapse analysis searches for entries with predictive power and reports one-sided testing on 50 generated sentences per group. The synthetic activation result is from one model and one synthetic task. The paper's monosemantic synapse and activation-sparsity findings do not test superposition, feature competition, or SAE properties.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results bearing on a listed version were reported. Other paper results, including network modularity and scaling-law comparisons, do not measure the features or geometry named by the versions.

untested.parts: All: overlapping, nearly orthogonal feature directions; sparsity-dependent transition; geometry.
All: capacity competition as the cause of polysemanticity.
All: non-capacity origins of polysemantic neurons.
All: features spread across neurons in LLMs; SAE recovery of sparse features.
All: completeness, stability and canonicity of SAE features.

record.verdict_notes: No superposition, SAE or Toy Models content appears. Table 3's remark about Transformer monosemantic neurons is a cited or generic statement, not a result. The modularity (Section 5.5) and model-merging results bear on no version.

versions.untested_parts: Whether overcomplete sparse features are stored as overlapping, nearly orthogonal directions; sparsity-dependent transitions and regular geometry.
Whether capacity pressure explains polysemantic neurons, or important features receive dedicated dimensions while others share.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise for other reasons or are insufficient evidence of superposition.
Whether features in LLMs are distributed across many neurons or whether SAEs recover sparse features.
Whether SAE features are complete, stable, canonical units of model representation.
Whether represented features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional.

rows.subject: BDH-GPU
rows.stage_stated: trained on about one epoch of En-Es, En-Pt, and En-Fr data (total 1.9B tokens)
rows.operation_detail: Measured Currency synapse values on currency-related versus contrast sentences; the synapse was selected for predictive power in separating concept-containing sentences from contrasts.

conditions.value: 50 ChatGPT-generated sentences relating to European currencies versus 50 European-politics sentences not mentioning currencies

rows.measure: One-sided Mann–Whitney U comparison of Currency synapse values
rows.value: Currency-related sentences received significantly higher values; U = 2368 with Uopt = 2500, p < 10−14; rank-biserial correlation = 0.86
rows.note: Reports semantic selectivity of a synapse, not superposition, capacity competition, or an SAE feature.
rows.check: Selection-based result: the synapse was chosen for its predictive power at separating concept sentences from contrasts, then tested on 50 vs 50 ChatGPT-generated sentences. It concerns a BDH attention-state entry, not a neuron or SAE feature, so it bears on no version.

rows.subject: BDH-GPU
rows.stage_stated: trained on a synthetic next-token prediction task
rows.operation_detail: Measured the fraction of nonzero neuron activations in layer 2 during memorization of the random word.

conditions.value: Fixed 13-letter warm-up followed by 8 repetitions of an 8-letter random word; pattern repeats every 13 + 8 · 8 = 77 letters

rows.measure: Fraction of neurons with nonzero y activation
rows.note: This measures activation sparsity in a BDH-GPU synthetic-task experiment, not sparse features or feature-overlap geometry.
rows.check: Neuron activation sparsity in a synthetic task. It does not measure feature sparsity or superposition.

conditions.value: Fixed 13-letter warm-up followed by 8 repetitions of an 8-letter random word; pattern repeats every 13 + 8 · 8 = 77 letters

rows.measure: Fraction of neurons with nonzero y activation
rows.note: The authors describe sparser layer-2 activation during repetition, but this does not test any listed superposition or feature-unit version.
rows.check: Same as r2. The baseline is the memorization phase of the same model, and no superposition measure is taken.
